```
export class LRUCache<T> {
  private cache = new Map<string, { value: T; expiresAt: number }>()
  private maxSize: number
  constructor(maxSize: number = 100) { this.maxSize = maxSize }
  get(key: string): T | undefined {
    const entry = this.cache.get(key)
    if (!entry) return undefined
    if (Date.now() > entry.expiresAt) { this.cache.delete(key); return undefined }
    this.cache.delete(key); this.cache.set(key, entry)
    return entry.value
  }
  set(key: string, value: T, ttlMs: number = 60000): void {
    if (this.cache.size >= this.maxSize) {
      const firstKey = this.cache.keys().next().value
      if (firstKey !== undefined) this.cache.delete(firstKey)
    }
    this.cache.set(key, { value, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttlMs })
  }
}

```

## What the cache module does

`src/cache.ts` exports a generic `LRUCache<T>` — an in-memory key-value store that combines two behaviors:

- **LRU (Least Recently Used) eviction** — bounds memory usage to `maxSize` entries (default 100).
- **TTL (Time-To-Live) expiration** — each entry carries an `expiresAt` timestamp and becomes invalid after its TTL (default 60,000 ms).

Internally it uses a `Map<string, { value: T; expiresAt: number }>`.

## Eviction strategy

When `set` is called and the cache is already at `maxSize`, it evicts the **first key in the Map** (`this.cache.keys().next().value`).

This is a true LRU policy because:
- `Map` preserves insertion order.
- `get` deletes and re-inserts an accessed entry, moving it to the **end** of the Map.
- Therefore the **front** of the Map is always the least recently used entry, which is exactly what gets evicted.

## What happens when a key expires

Expiration is handled **lazily** — only on `get`:

- If `Date.now() > entry.expiresAt`, the entry is deleted from the Map and `get` returns `undefined`.
- There is **no background sweeper**; expired entries are only removed when they are accessed (or when evicted by LRU pressure). Until then they still occupy a slot in the cache.

## Short summary

A generic LRU cache with TTL: `get` refreshes recency and lazily drops expired entries; `set` evicts the least recently used item when full. Expired keys are cleaned up on access rather than by a timer, so stale-but-unaccessed entries linger until evicted or read.
